questions.stem: A chemical factory worker presented with burning pain sensation in mouth and abdomen along with nausea, vomiting and blood in stool. Which poisoning is suspected in this case?
questions.solutionHtml:
Arsenic

Arsenic poisoning causes burning pain in the upper GI tract, Diarrhoea with blood, Nausea and vomiting.



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 33rd edition, Page number- 538.

questions.stem: A 48 year old male comes with injuries in hospital OPD. The examining doctor notices a lacerated wound of size 4×0.5 cm bone deep with blood clots over the scalp which was looking like an incised wound along with linear abrasion of size 2×0.5 cm below the nipple .What caused the lacerated injury over the scalp?

options.label: A
options.text: Overstretching of skin and subcutaneous tissue

options.label: C
options.text: Soft tissue is sandwiched between the weapon and underlying bone

options.label: D
options.text: Impact by semi sharp object with heavy force

questions.answerText: Soft tissue is sandwiched between the weapon and underlying bone
questions.solutionHtml:
Soft tissue is sandwiched between the weapon and underlying bone

Given case findings suggest presence of a split laceration that occurred due to the soft tissue being sandwiched between the weapon and underlying bone.



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 33rd edition, Page number- 191.

questions.stem: One friend murdered another because of having a common girlfriend by compressing his nostrils and mouth while sitting on his chest. What is this mechanism?
questions.solutionHtml:
Burking

Includes two processes: Homicidal Smothering (compressing his nostrils and mouth) and Traumatic Asphyxia (sitting on his chest).




KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 33rd edition, Page number- 364.

questions.stem: During resuscitation, a patient received intralipid 20%. What could have been the most probable cause for giving intralipid?
questions.solutionHtml:
LA toxicity

Intralipid is an antidote for Local Anaesthetic toxicity.



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 33rd edition, Page number-.380.

questions.stem: A case of hanging has come to the forensic department for autopsy. On examination a ligature mark covering about 1/3rd of the neck, protruded tongue, salivary stains, his right eye was open while left was close, both pupils dilated. The reason for the opened right eye?
questions.solutionHtml:
Cervical sympathetic chain

Given case scenario describes the term ‘Le Facies sympathique’  which is seen in cases of antemortem hanging along with ligature mark covering 1/3rd of neck thus confirming suicidal hanging. Maximum pressure is always exerted on the opposite side of the knot. Thus, due to pressure upon the cervical sympathetic, the eye on the same side of the knot remains open and both pupils are dilated.



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 33rd edition, Page number- 344, https://www.jaypeedigital.com/eReader/chapter/9788184487060/ch15

questions.stem: Patient was brought dead, with multiple small puncture wounds over right anterior chest wall, multiple abrasions and lacerations over left lower abdominal wall. What is the reason?
questions.solutionHtml:
Flying missiles

Triad of Punctate abrasions , bruises and punctate lacerations seen in  secondary blast/ explosion injuries caused by flying missiles generated by the bomb blast and known as Marshall’s triad.



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 33rd edition, Page number- 239-241.

questions.stem: A person had an injury on his thigh. On examination, there is soddened burn injury with erythema, blisters and red line of demarcation. What is most likely cause?
questions.solutionHtml:
Moist burn

Presence of sodden injury with erythema, blisters and red line of demarcation is typical of moist burn/scalds.



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 33rd edition, Page number- 329.
